_doc: Surface -> drift-sentinel manifest for the merge-time impacted-test gate. Each entry maps a SURFACE GLOB (repo-relative, '**' = any depth, '*' = one path segment) to the drift-sentinel test file(s) that guard that surface. A drift sentinel AST/rglob-scans a whole source tree (or a fixed source-file set) and compares it against a stored __fixtures__/*.json (or snapshot) — it never imports the app modules it guards, so impacted_tests.py's dotted-import reverse-dep scan cannot select it. Without this manifest such a sentinel runs only in the full promotion suite, so a drift-introducing change (e.g. a new websocket emitter or event_type) merges green on the task PR and only breaks weeks later at the automain->main promotion matrix. Registration here makes impacted_tests.resolve_impacted() select the sentinel whenever a changed path matches its surface. The merge gate treats every matched, on-disk sentinel as mandatory: its ordinary relevance budget remains capped at eight selectors, while the mandatory sentinel partition is carried past that cap exactly once per path. Choose globs conservatively: a whole-tree glob fires on every PR touching that tree (acceptable for a fast source-scan sentinel), but scope to specific files when the sentinel only scans a fixed source-file set.

surfaces.why: test_scripts_dir_resolution_guard.py AST-scans the WHOLE backend tree (every backend/**/*.py outside alembic/versions/) for hand-rolled repo-scripts resolution: a parent-directory walk that joins 'scripts', or a sys.path mutation that adds a scripts directory, without going through backend/testing/repo_scripts_path.resolve_scripts_dir. It imports nothing that a new offender would import, so the dotted-import reverse-dep scan can never select it: the offender is a brand-new literal path expression in an arbitrary module. Without this registration the guard runs only in the full promotion suite, which is exactly the #17738 shape -- the drift merges green on the task PR and surfaces at the automain->main promotion matrix, where a red CLOSES the PR and deletes its release branch. The surface is the whole backend tree because that is literally the corpus the guard scans; the cost is bounded (the guard prefilters on source text and parses ~47 of ~1231 files, ~3s). Deliberately NOT added to scripts/test-backend.sh STANDALONE_ARGS: that lane and the ordinary sharded backend lanes both pass LANE_HANG_DETECTOR_SECONDS (backend/testing/test_harness_timeout_budgets.py) as pytest's --timeout, and this guard reads the whole backend tree over a Docker bind mount, which is the harness-budget-inversion flake shape. The sharded backend lanes collect it at the promotion gate, and this registration covers the task PR.

test_no_comment_cites_a_superseded_lane_timeout reads backend/testing/*.py, backend/app/**/*.py, scripts/*.py and scripts/test-backend.sh as TEXT, looking for a literal '--timeout=<digits>' that disagrees with LANE_HANG_DETECTOR_SECONDS. The thing it polices is a COMMENT, so there is no import edge to it by construction and the dotted-import reverse-dep scan can never select this file. Unregistered, the guard would run only in the full promotion suite: prose rot merges green on the task PR and reds the automain->main promotion PR, which then CLOSES and deletes its release branch -- strictly worse than the rot it polices. Registration is what makes this guard net-positive rather than a delayed promotion-killer. The surface is the whole backend tree because that is most of the corpus it reads; the scan is one read_text per file with no ast.parse, measured 0.69s for the three pinning tests together. KNOWN GAP, deliberate: scripts/*.py is scanned but is NOT registered as a surface here. A non-backend glob would make impacted_tests.corpus_lane_required_sentinels demand a STANDALONE_ARGS seat for this whole MODULE, and the module's other tests drive scripts/test-backend.sh's _run_pytest through real bash subprocesses -- 72.91s for its 20 tests on a native Windows checkout, and the corpus lane runs over a Docker-on-Windows bind mount where that gets worse. A scripts-only diff that introduces a stale citation is therefore caught at the promotion gate rather than on the task PR. Widen this only together with that roster seat, and measure the module on the bind mount first.

test_websocket_emitter_inventory.py AST-scans the ENTIRE backend/app tree (read_app_sources -> app_dir.rglob('*.py')) against __fixtures__/websocket_event_inventory_v1.json and imports only backend/testing helpers, so a new emitter in any app module never selects it by import. test_direction_referential_guard.py rglobs the whole app tree for new Direction.criterion_keys writers (against KNOWN_GUARDED_WRITERS); it imports app.direction_referential_guard, so it is only import-selectable when THAT module changes, never when a new writer appears in an unrelated file. test_operator_workbench_contracts.py::test_websocket_emitter_inventory_covers_current_emitters rglobs the SAME whole app tree ((BACKEND_ROOT / "app").rglob("*.py")) against the hand-kept WEBSOCKET_EMITTER_INVENTORY dict in backend/app/workbench_contracts.py; it imports app.workbench_contracts, so the reverse-dep scan selects it only when THAT one module changes, never when the new emitter lands in some other file — the exact hole that let backend/app/recovery_evaluating_prless_hold.py reach the promotion matrix unrecorded. Registered as a NODE ID rather than a whole file: the module's other tests need the client/db_session fixtures, so a whole-file registration would ERROR on a missing fixture under the --no-postgres route instead of reporting drift. All three must run whenever any app source changes. (test_websocket_emitter_inventory.py and the node id above are ALSO in scripts/test-backend.sh STANDALONE_ARGS; these registrations are additive and complementary.)

test_event_type_invariants.py regex-extracts event_type="..." literals from a FIXED source-file set and compares them against event_type_snapshot.json. It reads the files by path (never imports the modules), so a new/renamed event_type merges undetected unless the sentinel is selected. It is NOT in STANDALONE_ARGS. Scoped to the exact files the sentinel scans rather than the whole tree so it does not fire on every app PR.
Second source file in test_event_type_invariants.py's fixed source_paths set (event_type literals for capability trial verdicts). Same rationale as backend/app/notification_dispatch.py.

All three sentinels read the backend test INVENTORY itself (estate_inventory.iter_backend_test_files -> backend/testing/test_*.py) instead of importing anything the changed file imports, so adding, deleting or renaming a backend test file is invisible to the reverse-dep scan: it selects the changed test file and never the guards over the inventory that file belongs to. test_test_durations_freshness.py checks the coverage fraction and re-derives every collected node id to reject stale entries in backend/.test_durations; test_test_estate_ranked_queue.py set-compares the collected inventory against test-estate-ranked-queue.md; test_conversational_workday_protection.py pins an exact per-file test COUNT for the nineteen backend/testing paths in conversational_workday_manifest.json's PROTECT list. This single glob is deliberately broader than that nineteen-file subset: the PROTECT list is edited far more often than it is stable, so nineteen literal globs here would need a manifest edit every time it moves and would fail OPEN when someone forgot. The cost is bounded and already paid elsewhere - all three are scripts/test-backend.sh STANDALONE_ARGS members that any backend/ change already runs through the static corpus; this registration additionally puts them in the targeted merge lane so the failure is attributed to the PR that caused it.

The artifact the sentinel validates. It is not a .py file at all, so neither the reverse-dep scan nor the conventional test_<module>.py rule can reach its guard; without this entry a regenerated or hand-edited .test_durations runs no check on .test_durations.

test_outlier_cap_matches_durations_quality reads this file BY PATH (it parses the source to recover the outlier cap) rather than importing it, so a cap change here silently desynchronises the two definitions. Scoped to the exact file, not scripts/**, for the same reason as the scripts/test_runner_isolation.py entry below.

The derived artifact the sentinel set-compares against the collected inventory. It is a root-level markdown file: it matches no STATIC_PATH_PREFIXES entry and sits in no import graph, so before this registration a hand-edit to the queue was the one change to it that ran none of its own guards. Repair command: python3 scripts/generate_test_estate_ranked_queue.py --write.

The sentinel loads this generator through importlib from a resolved repository root, never as a dotted module, so the reverse-dep scan cannot connect the two. Scoped to the exact file, not scripts/**.

Both sentinels derive their expected inventory from iter_backend_test_files / is_vitest_test_path here. The module lives under backend/testing/, not backend/app/, so impacted_tests.py's reverse-dep scan (scoped to backend/app/<...>.py -> app.* importers) never even considers it a changed module - the same gap as the backend/testing/check_size_limits.py entry below.

test_test_estate_ranked_queue.py set-compares the Vitest inventory (estate_inventory.is_vitest_test_path) against test-estate-ranked-queue.md, so it fires only when a Vitest test file is ADDED or DELETED. Scoped to the five test-file globs the inventory predicate actually collects rather than to admin-ui/** so a routine component edit does not pay the guard.
Second Vitest test-file extension collected by is_vitest_test_path for the admin-ui suite. Same rationale as admin-ui/src/**/*.test.ts.
is_vitest_test_path also collects admin-ui/eslint-rules/**/*.test.{js,ts}; a rule test added there is ranked-queue inventory and nothing under admin-ui/src/ need change with it.
Second eslint-rules test extension collected by is_vitest_test_path. Same rationale as admin-ui/eslint-rules/**/*.test.js.
The agent Vitest suite's collected set (is_vitest_test_path('agent', ...) = src/**/*.test.ts). Same add/delete-only firing rationale as the admin-ui globs above.

The manifest the sentinel validates. It is JSON, so no import edge and no conventional test_<module>.py rule reaches it: editing the PROTECT list - the change most likely to break the guard - previously selected nothing that checks the PROTECT list.

test_migration_chain.py::test_migration_files_do_not_import_app_modules AST-scans every migration file in alembic/versions/ for app.* imports — a class of defect (#15100, 0621/0626) that causes ImportError in the promotion apply gate when migration files are executed in the serving process. Migration files never import backend/testing helpers and are not in backend/app/, so the dotted-import reverse-dep scan never selects this guard. Register here so any change to a migration file runs the guard at merge time.

test_migration_0621_safe_encrypt_backfill.py loads the migration via importlib rather than importing it as an app.* module, so the dotted-import reverse-dep scan cannot select it. Register here so that changes to the migration body (e.g. inlining field_encryption helpers) cause the acceptance tests to run at the task PR rather than only at the promotion matrix.
Same rationale as 0621: test_migration_0626_safe_encrypt_backfill.py loads the migration via importlib; register here so migration body changes trigger the acceptance tests at the task PR.

check_size_limits.py lives under backend/testing/, not backend/app/, so impacted_tests.py's reverse-dep scan (scoped to backend/app/<...>.py -> app.* importers) never even considers it as a changed module, regardless of what test_size_limits_checker.py imports (it does `from testing import check_size_limits`). Register here so a change to the checker itself always runs its own test file at merge time instead of only at the promotion matrix.

test_vitest_durations_freshness.py reads admin-ui/.test_durations.json and rglobs admin-ui/src (and eslint-rules/) for the committed Vitest test inventory it must match. It imports nothing under backend/app or backend/testing, and the changed files it cares about live entirely outside backend/, so neither the dotted-import reverse-dep scan nor STATIC_PATH_PREFIXES in scripts/static_release_guard.py can select it. A PR confined to admin-ui/ previously merged with a stale duration artifact undetected until the promotion matrix forced every guard on.

test_conversational_workday_protection.py validates conversational_workday_manifest.json's PROTECT list, which names files under admin-ui/src. Same selection gap as the durations sentinel: no backend/app import, no backend/ prefix match.
Same rationale as admin-ui/** above, for the agent/ Vitest suite: test_vitest_durations_freshness.py reads agent/.test_durations.json and rglobs agent/src for the committed test inventory.
conversational_workday_manifest.json's PROTECT list also names files under agent/src; same selection gap as the admin-ui/src/** entry above.

conversational_workday_manifest.json's PROTECT list names this exact file. Scoped to the file itself (not a scripts/** wildcard) so it does not widen STATIC_PATH_PREFIXES's deliberately narrow scripts/ scope (e.g. scripts/test-backend.sh.bak must stay out of scope, per test_static_scope_matches_path_boundaries).
conversational_workday_manifest.json's PROTECT list names this exact file. Same scoping rationale as scripts/test_runner_isolation.py above.

SIZE-GUARDRAIL LEFT SHIFT. The module-size guardrail (module_size_limits.json caps + the 1500-line uncapped coverage threshold) was enforced against the LIVE TREE only by test_invariants.py, which runs in the ci.yml backend matrix -- and ci.yml's pull_request trigger is `branches: [main]`, so an automain PR never runs it. The only workflow an automain PR does get is guard-data.yml, whose Derived-artifacts job replaces the standalone roster wholesale via BLUEPRINT_STATIC_GUARD_SELECTORS (no size scan in that list) and whose Impacted-backend-tests job runs only what this manifest selects. Before this entry NO glob mapped a governed source surface to any live-tree size scan, so a size breach first turned red on the automain->main promotion PR -- the worst place for it, since a red promotion PR usually CLOSES and deletes its release branch. Proven live, not theoretical: PR #17966 took backend/testing/test_impacted_tests.py from 1431 to 1522 lines past the uncapped threshold and merged into automain green. backend/app is the 'backend' section's source root, so any change here can breach a cap. The sentinel imports check_size_limits, not the modules it scans, so the dotted-import reverse-dep scan can never select it for an arbitrary app file.

backend/testing is the 'testing' section's source root and the surface the proven breach (test_impacted_tests.py at 1522 uncapped lines, merged green into automain) actually landed on. Registered as **/*.py rather than test_*.py because the section scans every .py under the root, helpers included.

The cap ledger itself. Lowering a cap, or deleting an entry, turns a previously-clean file into a violation without touching a single source file, so the gate has to re-run on an edit to this artifact. It is not a .py file, so neither the reverse-dep scan nor the test_<module>.py convention can reach it.

agent/src is the 'agent' section's source root. A PR confined to agent/ contains no backend Python at all, so the reverse-dep scan selects nothing and only this registration (plus the standalone roster seat it forces) puts a size scan on that diff.
admin-ui/src is the 'frontend' section's source root (.ts/.tsx, excluding *.test.ts(x) and *.d.ts). Same selection gap as agent/src/** above.

scripts/ is the 'scripts' section's source root, with 17 capped modules and release-critical logic. A scripts/**-shaped glob is safe here where the older conversational-workday entries deliberately used exact filenames: scripts/ is ALREADY a static_release_guard STATIC_PATH_PREFIXES member derived from conversational_workday_manifest.json (test_static_scope_matches_path_boundaries asserts scripts/test-backend.sh.bak is in scope), so this widens nothing there. Registering these three non-backend surfaces is what makes impacted_tests.corpus_lane_required_sentinels demand a STANDALONE_ARGS seat for this sentinel -- deliberate, and paid for honestly: the scan is a corpus walk whose cost is file I/O, measured 3x on each filesystem it runs on -- ~2.6s with the repo on a Linux filesystem (what CI does) but 78-103s across a Docker-on-Windows bind mount (what ./check test does on a Windows dev box). It therefore carries an explicit @pytest.mark.timeout(120) so its budget is stated at the test rather than inherited from whatever the lane happens to pass -- LANE_HANG_DETECTOR_SECONDS (backend/testing/test_harness_timeout_budgets.py) is a hang detector for the lane as a whole, not a performance budget for this scan, and the marker keeps a slow filesystem from being reported as a size defect either way. See the module docstring for both measurements.
